---
title: "Same default, different J"
subtitle: "Catalog M-01 and M-02 · paper Figure 2"
description: "A fixed Gamma default on alpha implies an expected number of clusters that grows with J, and a majority-mass tail that does not."
toc: false
---

A default hyperprior on the concentration parameter, such as the "vague" Gamma(1, 1),
is usually chosen once and reused for every study. In Chinese-restaurant terms, alpha is
the pseudo-count of "tables not yet seen": the chance that the n-th unit opens a new
table is alpha / (alpha + n - 1). The same alpha therefore implies *more* tables when
there are more units, roughly E(alpha) log J. The size of the table a random unit joins
does not work that way: its tail, Pr(W_SB > .5) = (b / (b + log 2))^a, involves no J at all.

## How to read it

- **Panel A.** Under Gamma(1, 1) the expected number of clusters is 4.16 at J = 50,
  4.84 at J = 100 and 7.82 at J = 2000: the same "vague" default says something different
  about heterogeneity in a 50-school study and in a 2000-site registry.
- **Panel B.** The majority-mass tail is flat: .591 for Gamma(1, 1) at every J.
- **Panel C (M-02).** The "conservative" literature defaults Gamma(1, 3) and Gamma(2, 4)
  have a smaller E(alpha), so they imply fewer clusters, but a *larger* chance that a
  randomly chosen unit sits in a cluster holding more than half of the population:
  .812 and .726, against .591 for Gamma(1, 1). Switch **Focus** to compare.
- The dotted guides mark the three applications in the paper: Bangert-Drowns (J = 48
  studies), STAR (J = 79 schools) and the vocabulary checklist (N = 500 respondents).

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
K_J is the number of fitted components (occupied clusters) among the J units.
W_SB is the size-biased first weight: the share of the cluster that a randomly chosen
unit belongs to. It is not the largest weight. The 90% band is computed live for
J ≤ 500; beyond that it is read from values precomputed with the DPprior R package.
:::

Try a custom Gamma(a, b) with the sliders, or open the standalone version:
[embed/defaults-drift.html](../../embed/defaults-drift.html) (for example
`?a=1&b=3` starts the custom prior at Gamma(1, 3)).
